import json
import os
import shutil
import tempfile
import unittest

from tests.helpers import load_tool

ct = load_tool("check-transcripts.py")
SID = "11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555"
BANNER_OK = ("=== small-beeps session banner v1 ===\nrole: clean\nstatus: OK\n"
             "=== end of banner ===\n")


def hook(stdout, code=0):
    return {"type": "attachment", "attachment": {
        "type": "hook_success" if code == 0 else "hook_non_blocking_error",
        "hookEvent": "SessionStart", "hookName": "SessionStart:startup",
        "stdout": stdout, "stderr": "", "exitCode": code}}


def call(name, **inp):
    return {"type": "assistant", "message": {"content": [
        {"type": "tool_use", "name": name, "input": inp}]}}


class TranscriptTest(unittest.TestCase):
    """Requirements: R-CLEAN-1, R-CLEAN-3, R-CLEAN-5"""

    def setUp(self):
        self.dir = tempfile.mkdtemp()

    def tearDown(self):
        shutil.rmtree(self.dir)

    def write(self, entries, role="clean", sid=SID, note=True):
        name = "2026-10-21-%s-%s" % (role, sid)
        with open(os.path.join(self.dir, name + ".jsonl"), "w") as f:
            for e in entries:
                f.write(json.dumps(e) + "\n")
        if note:
            open(os.path.join(self.dir, name + ".REDACTIONS.md"), "w").close()
        return os.path.join(self.dir, name + ".jsonl")

    def problems(self, path):
        return ct.check_session(path)[0]

    def test_clean_session_with_banner_passes(self):
        p = self.write([hook(BANNER_OK), call("Read", file_path="/x/docs/PLAN.md"),
                        call("Bash", command="git status")])
        self.assertEqual(self.problems(p), [])

    def test_missing_banner_fails(self):
        p = self.write([call("Read", file_path="README.md")])
        self.assertTrue(any("no SessionStart banner" in x for x in self.problems(p)))

    def test_mismatch_fails(self):
        bad = BANNER_OK.replace("status: OK", "status: CONFIG MISMATCH")
        p = self.write([hook(bad, 1)])
        self.assertTrue(any("CONFIG MISMATCH" in x for x in self.problems(p)))

    def test_first_session_is_exempt_only_by_id(self):
        sid = next(iter(ct.EXEMPT_NO_BANNER))
        p = self.write([call("Read", file_path="README.md")], sid=sid)
        self.assertEqual(self.problems(p), [])

    def test_forbidden_reads_fetches_and_commands_fail(self):
        cases = [
            call("Read", file_path="/w/vendor/emulator/src/lib.rs"),
            call("Read", file_path="./harness/src/main.rs"),
            call("Grep", pattern="lcd", path="/w/fm1-sid"),
            call("WebFetch", url="https://github.com/hugelton/Felucca"),
            call("WebFetch", url="https://thefirmwarehub.com/x"),
            call("Bash", command="git clone https://github.com/zvenson/dinghy"),
            call("Bash", command="cat ../fm1-emu/crates/fm1-soc/src/lcd.rs"),
            call("Glob", pattern="**/probes/lcdtest.c"),
            call("Bash", command="ls harness"),
            call("Bash", command="cat vendor/emulator/README"),
            call("WebFetch", url="https://github.com/AL-255/FM-1-RE/tree/main/firmware-images"),
        ]
        for c in cases:
            p = self.write([hook(BANNER_OK), c])
            self.assertTrue(any("forbidden" in x for x in self.problems(p)), json.dumps(c))

    def test_reviewed_hits_pass_only_for_that_exact_call(self):
        c = call("Bash", command="printf 'leaves out vendor/emulator/' > msg.txt")
        c["message"]["content"][0]["id"] = "toolu_1"
        p = self.write([hook(BANNER_OK), c])
        rule = "vendor/emulator/ (spec side)"
        self.assertTrue(self.problems(p))
        ok = ct.check_session(p, {(SID, "toolu_1", rule): "writes a message only"})
        self.assertEqual(ok[0], [])
        self.assertTrue(any("REVIEWED toolu_1" in l for l in ok[1]))
        self.assertTrue(ct.check_session(p, {(SID, "toolu_2", rule): "other call"})[0])
        self.assertTrue(ct.check_session(p, {("other", "toolu_1", rule): "other session"})[0])

    def test_reviewed_file_needs_a_reason(self):
        with open(os.path.join(self.dir, "REVIEWED.json"), "w") as f:
            json.dump({"reviewed": [{"session": SID, "tool_use_id": "t", "rule": "r"}]}, f)
        with self.assertRaises(SystemExit):
            ct.load_reviewed(self.dir)

    def test_writing_about_forbidden_material_is_not_a_read(self):
        p = self.write([hook(BANNER_OK),
                        call("Write", file_path="/w/CONTRIBUTING.md",
                             content="never open vendor/emulator/ or Felucca")])
        self.assertEqual(self.problems(p), [])

    def test_words_that_are_not_paths_pass(self):
        p = self.write([hook(BANNER_OK),
                        call("Bash", command="python3 tools/check-transcripts.py"),
                        call("Grep", pattern="harnessing", path="docs")])
        self.assertEqual(self.problems(p), [])

    def test_spec_side_may_read_emulator_source(self):
        p = self.write([hook(BANNER_OK.replace("clean", "spec")),
                        call("Read", file_path="/w/vendor/emulator/src/lib.rs")], role="spec")
        self.assertEqual(self.problems(p), [])

    def test_subagent_transcripts_are_checked(self):
        p = self.write([hook(BANNER_OK)])
        sub = p[:-len(".jsonl")] + ".subagents"
        os.makedirs(sub)
        with open(os.path.join(sub, "agent-1.jsonl"), "w") as f:
            f.write(json.dumps(call("Read", file_path="/w/harness/src/x.rs")) + "\n")
        self.assertTrue(any("forbidden" in x for x in self.problems(p)))

    def test_redaction_note_required(self):
        p = self.write([hook(BANNER_OK)], note=False)
        self.assertTrue(any("redaction note" in x for x in self.problems(p)))

    def test_bad_file_name_fails(self):
        with open(os.path.join(self.dir, "notes.jsonl"), "w") as f:
            f.write("{}\n")
        self.assertTrue(self.problems(os.path.join(self.dir, "notes.jsonl")))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

import unittest

from tests.helpers import ROOT, load_tool

ar = load_tool("archive-session.py")
ct = load_tool("check-transcripts.py")

# Built at run time so this file never contains a token-shaped string.
TOKEN = "gh" + "o_" + "A1b2C3d4" * 5
KEY = "sk-" + "ant-" + "x" * 30
PRIVATE = ("-----BEGIN OPENSSH " + "PRIVATE KEY-----\\nabc\\n-----END OPENSSH "
           + "PRIVATE KEY-----")


class ArchiveTest(unittest.TestCase):
    """Requirements: R-CLEAN-3"""

    def setUp(self):
        self.dir = tempfile.mkdtemp()

    def tearDown(self):
        shutil.rmtree(self.dir)

    def test_redact_line(self):
        counts = {}
        line = json.dumps({
            "text": "token %s key %s mail [REDACTED:email] keep noreply@anthropic.com "
                    "path ~/Development/x tmp /tmp/claude-UID/a"
                    % (TOKEN, KEY),
            "ownerAccountUuid": "abc-123"}) + "\n"
        line = line.replace("PLACEHOLDER", "")
        out = ar.redact_line(line, counts)
        json.loads(out)
        for gone in (TOKEN, KEY, "[REDACTED:email]", "~", "claude-501", "abc-123"):
            self.assertNotIn(gone, out)
        self.assertIn("noreply@anthropic.com", out)
        self.assertIn("~/Development/x", out)

    def test_private_key_in_json_string(self):
        line = json.dumps({"t": "x"}).replace('"x"', '"%s"' % PRIVATE) + "\n"
        counts = {}
        out = ar.redact_line(line, counts)
        self.assertNotIn("PRIVATE KEY-----\\nabc", out)
        json.loads(out)

    def test_archive_end_to_end_then_check(self):
        sid = "aaaaaaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddd-eeeeeeeeeeee"
        src_dir = os.path.join(self.dir, "projects")
        os.makedirs(os.path.join(src_dir, sid, "subagents"))
        src = os.path.join(src_dir, sid + ".jsonl")
        banner = ("=== small-beeps session banner v1 ===\nstatus: OK\n")
        with open(src, "w") as f:
            f.write(json.dumps({"type": "attachment", "timestamp": "2026-10-22T01:02:03Z",
                                "attachment": {"hookEvent": "SessionStart", "exitCode": 0,
                                               "stdout": banner}}) + "\n")
            f.write(json.dumps({"type": "user", "message": {"content": "hi " + TOKEN}}) + "\n")
            f.write(json.dumps({"type": "user", "message": {"content":
                "cwd ~/x; drwxr-xr-x 3 [REDACTED:user] staff; host [REDACTED:host]"}}) + "\n")
        with open(os.path.join(src_dir, sid, "subagents", "agent-a.jsonl"), "w") as f:
            f.write(json.dumps({"type": "assistant", "message": {"content": []}}) + "\n")
        out = os.path.join(self.dir, "sessions")
        subprocess.run([sys.executable, os.path.join(ROOT, "tools", "archive-session.py"),
                        src, "--role", "clean", "--out", out], check=True,
                       stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL)
        name = "2026-10-22-clean-" + sid
        with open(os.path.join(out, name + ".jsonl")) as f:
            text = f.read()
        for gone in (TOKEN, "[REDACTED:user]", "[REDACTED:host]"):
            self.assertNotIn(gone, text)
        self.assertTrue(os.path.exists(os.path.join(out, name + ".REDACTIONS.md")))
        self.assertTrue(os.path.exists(os.path.join(out, name + ".subagents", "agent-a.jsonl")))
        self.assertEqual(ct.check_session(os.path.join(out, name + ".jsonl"))[0], [])
        # Archiving the same session twice is refused.
        again = subprocess.run([sys.executable, os.path.join(ROOT, "tools", "archive-session.py"),
                                src, "--role", "clean", "--out", out],
                               stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
        self.assertNotEqual(again.returncode, 0)

    def test_settings_local_json_is_not_a_host_name(self):
        out = ar.redact_line(json.dumps({"t": "see .claude/settings.local.json"}) + "\n", {})
        self.assertIn("settings.local.json", out)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

import importlib.util
import os

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))


def load_tool(filename):
    path = os.path.join(ROOT, "tools", filename)
    name = filename.replace("-", "_").replace(".py", "")
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, path)
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return module

# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
import json
import os
import shutil
import tempfile
import unittest

from tests.helpers import ROOT, load_tool

dl = load_tool("check-deny-lists.py")
CONFIG = os.path.join(ROOT, "config", "claude")


class DenyListTest(unittest.TestCase):
    """Requirements: R-CLEAN-4"""

    def setUp(self):
        self.dir = tempfile.mkdtemp()
        for n in os.listdir(CONFIG):
            shutil.copyfile(os.path.join(CONFIG, n), os.path.join(self.dir, n))

    def tearDown(self):
        shutil.rmtree(self.dir)

    def edit(self, name, fn):
        p = os.path.join(self.dir, name)
        with open(p) as f:
            data = json.load(f)
        fn(data)
        with open(p, "w") as f:
            json.dump(data, f)

    def test_committed_configs_pass(self):
        self.assertEqual(dl.check(CONFIG), [])

    def test_clean_config_keeps_the_handmade_rules_unchanged(self):
        with open(os.path.join(CONFIG, "handmade-settings.json")) as f:
            handmade = json.load(f)["permissions"]["deny"]
        with open(os.path.join(CONFIG, "clean.json")) as f:
            clean = json.load(f)["permissions"]["deny"]
        self.assertEqual(clean[:len(handmade)], handmade)

    def test_dropping_any_entry_fails(self):
        for role in ("clean", "spec"):
            with open(os.path.join(CONFIG, role + ".json")) as f:
                rules = json.load(f)["permissions"]["deny"]
            for rule in rules:
                self.setUp()
                self.edit(role + ".json",
                          lambda d: d["permissions"]["deny"].remove(rule))
                self.assertTrue(dl.check(self.dir), "%s %s" % (role, rule))

    def test_dropping_from_the_baseline_fails(self):
        self.edit("deny-baseline.json", lambda d: d["spec"].pop())
        self.assertTrue(dl.check(self.dir))

    def test_adding_an_entry_passes(self):
        self.edit("spec.json", lambda d: d["permissions"]["deny"].append("WebFetch(domain:example.org)"))
        self.assertEqual(dl.check(self.dir), [])

    def test_missing_banner_hook_fails(self):
        self.edit("clean.json", lambda d: d.pop("hooks"))
        self.assertTrue(dl.check(self.dir))

    def test_changed_handmade_file_fails(self):
        with open(os.path.join(self.dir, "handmade-settings.json"), "a") as f:
            f.write("\n")
        self.assertTrue(dl.check(self.dir))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

def _commit_range():
    return os.environ.get("COMMIT_RANGE") or "..HEAD"


# Each check: id, title, requirement IDs, and either a command (list, or a
# function returning one, run from the repository root) or an internal
# function name. "records_only" checks run only with --with-merge.
CHECKS = [
    {"id": "C-UNIT", "title": "Unit tests of the tools",
     "reqs": ["R-PROC-1", "R-PROC-4", "R-REC-1", "R-CLEAN-3", "R-CLEAN-4", "R-PUB-1"],
     "cmd": [PY, "-m", "unittest", "discover", "-s", "tests", "-t", ".", "-v"]},
    {"id": "C-REUSE", "title": "reuse lint (SPDX licence and copyright on every file)",
     "reqs": ["R-LIC-1", "R-LIC-2"], "cmd": ["reuse", "lint"]},
    {"id": "C-COMMIT-MSG", "title": "Commit messages follow .gitmessage",
     "reqs": ["R-PROC-1"],
     "cmd": lambda: [PY, "-I", "tools/check-commit-msg.py", "--range", _commit_range()]},
    {"id": "C-LOW-PROFILE", "title": "Low profile: name, description, topics, README",
     "reqs": ["R-PUB-1"], "cmd": _low_profile_cmd},
    {"id": "C-SECRETS", "title": "No secrets in tracked files",
     "reqs": ["R-PUB-2"], "cmd": [PY, "-I", "tools/check-tracked.py", "secrets"]},
    {"id": "C-NO-TOOLCHAIN", "title": "No toolchain parts or binaries tracked",
     "reqs": ["R-REPRO-1"], "cmd": [PY, "-I", "tools/check-tracked.py", "no-toolchain"]},
    {"id": "C-DENY-LISTS", "title": "Claude Code deny lists never drop an entry",
     "reqs": ["R-CLEAN-4"], "cmd": [PY, "-I", "tools/check-deny-lists.py"]},
    {"id": "C-TRANSCRIPTS", "title": "Archived session transcripts: banners and forbidden material",
     "reqs": ["R-CLEAN-1", "R-CLEAN-3", "R-CLEAN-5"],
     "cmd": [PY, "-I", "tools/check-transcripts.py"]},
    {"id": "C-SDK-PIN", "title": "Vendored SDK files match the pinned commit",
     "reqs": ["R-REPRO-5", "R-LIC-2"], "cmd": ["sh", "tools/fetch-sdk.sh", "--verify"]},
    {"id": "C-IMAGE", "title": "Build container (pinned base, toolchain SHA-256 checked)",
     "reqs": ["R-REPRO-1", "R-REPRO-2"], "cmd": ["sh", "tools/build.sh", "image"]},
    {"id": "C-BUILD-A", "title": "Build A in a fresh container (source at /mnt/small-beeps-src)",
     "reqs": ["R-REPRO-3", "R-BUILD-1"],
     "cmd": lambda: ["sh", "tools/build.sh", "build", "--out", os.path.join(OUT, "build-a")]},
    {"id": "C-BUILD-B", "title": "Build B in a fresh container (source at another path)",
     "reqs": ["R-REPRO-3"],
     "cmd": lambda: ["sh", "tools/build.sh", "build", "--out", os.path.join(OUT, "build-b"),
                     "--src-mount", "/tmp/elsewhere/small-beeps-src-b"]},
    {"id": "C-DETERMINISM", "title": "Builds A and B are byte-identical",
     "reqs": ["R-REPRO-3"], "internal": "determinism"},
    {"id": "C-MERGE", "title": "Signed owner merge of a pull request that passed CI",
     "reqs": ["R-PROC-2"], "records_only": True,
     "cmd": lambda: [PY, "-I", "tools/check-merge.py", git("rev-parse", "HEAD")]},
]

OUT = ""


def git(*args):
    try:
        return subprocess.run(["git", "-C", ROOT] + list(args), check=True,
                              "GITHUB_WORKFLOW", "GITHUB_EVENT_NAME", "GITHUB_REF",
                              "GITHUB_SHA", "RUNNER_OS", "RUNNER_ARCH", "ImageOS",
                              "ImageVersion")}
    return env


def requirements_table():
    rows = []
    with open(os.path.join(ROOT, "docs", "REQUIREMENTS.md"), encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for line in f:
            m = re.match(r"^\| (R-[A-Z]+-\d+) \|(.*)\|(.*)\|(.*)\|\s*$", line)
            if m:
                rows.append({"id": m.group(1), "since": m.group(3).strip(),
                             "checked_by": m.group(4).strip()})
    return rows


def traceability(checks, defined=None):
    """requirement -> checks -> result. A requirement passes only if every
    defined check that covers it ran and passed; checks that didn't run in
    this record are named."""
    defined = CHECKS if defined is None else defined
    ran = {c["id"]: c["result"] for c in checks}
    table = []
    for req in requirements_table():
        mine = [c["id"] for c in defined if req["id"] in c["reqs"]]
        results = [ran[c] for c in mine if c in ran]
        missing = [c for c in mine if c not in ran]
        if not mine:
            result = "not machine-checked (%s)" % req["checked_by"]
        elif "FAIL" in results:
            result = "FAIL"
        elif not results:
            result = "not run in this record (%s)" % ", ".join(missing)
        elif missing:
            result = "PASS (%s not run)" % ", ".join(missing)
        else:
            result = "PASS"
        table.append({"requirement": req["id"], "checks": mine, "result": result})
    return table


def write_markdown(report, path):
    L = ["# Test record %s" % report["commit"][:12], "",
         "- Commit: `%s`" % report["commit"],
19:    """Requirements: R-PROC-4, R-REC-1"""
44:                self.assertRegex(doc, r"Requirements: R-[A-Z]+-\d+", path)

def requirements_table():

def traceability(checks, defined=None):
    """requirement -> checks -> result. A requirement passes only if every
    defined check that covers it ran and passed; checks that didn't run in
    this record are named."""
    defined = CHECKS if defined is None else defined
    ran = {c["id"]: c["result"] for c in checks}
    table = []
    for req in requirements_table():
        mine = [c["id"] for c in defined if req["id"] in c["reqs"]]
        results = [ran[c] for c in mine if c in ran]
        missing = [c for c in mine if c not in ran]

        elif missing:

        else:
            result = "PASS"
        table.append({"requirement": req["id"], "checks": mine, "result": result})

#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
#
# Builds everything inside the pinned build container (tools/Dockerfile).
#
#   tools/build.sh image                      build the container image
#   tools/build.sh image-tag                  print its tag
#   tools/build.sh build --out DIR [--src-mount PATH]
#                                             build in a fresh container,
#                                             outputs and SHA256SUMS in DIR
#   tools/build.sh inside SRC OUT             (runs inside the container)
#
# Builds are deterministic (R-REPRO-3): fixed SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH (set in the
# image), no network, relative source paths with -fdebug-prefix-map, sorted
# output lists, and a check that no output contains the source mount path.
set -eu

ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
PLATFORM=linux/amd64

sha256() {
    if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then sha256sum "$1" | cut -d' ' -f1
    else shasum -a 256 "$1" | cut -d' ' -f1; fi
}

image_tag() {
    echo "small-beeps-build:$(sha256 "$ROOT/tools/Dockerfile" | cut -c1-16)"
}

cmd_image() {
    # No build context: the Dockerfile fetches everything it needs.
    docker build --platform "$PLATFORM" -t "$(image_tag)" - < "$ROOT/tools/Dockerfile"
    docker image inspect --format 'image {{.Id}}' "$(image_tag)"
}

cmd_build() {
    out="" src_mount=/mnt/small-beeps-src
    while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
        case "$1" in
            --out) out=$2; shift 2 ;;
            --src-mount) src_mount=$2; shift 2 ;;
            *) echo "unknown option $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
        esac
    done
    [ -n "$out" ] || { echo "build: --out DIR is required" >&2; exit 2; }
    tag=$(image_tag)
    docker image inspect "$tag" >/dev/null 2>&1 || cmd_image
    rm -rf "$out"
    mkdir -p "$out"
    out=$(cd "$out" && pwd)
    docker run --rm --platform "$PLATFORM" --network none \
        --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" \
        -v "$ROOT:$src_mount:ro" -v "$out:/out" -w "$src_mount" \
        "$tag" sh "$src_mount/tools/build.sh" inside "$src_mount" /out
    cat "$out/SHA256SUMS"
}

cmd_inside() {
    src=$1 out=$2
    cd "$src"
    CFLAGS="-target pi32v2 -std=c11 -ffreestanding -nostdlib -Os -g
            -Wall -Wextra -Werror -fdebug-prefix-map=$src=."
    clang --version | head -1
    ld --version | head -1
    echo "SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=$SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH"
    set -x
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    clang $CFLAGS -c firmware/src/placeholder.c -o "$out/placeholder.o"
    ld -nostdlib -e placeholder -o "$out/placeholder.elf" "$out/placeholder.o"
    set +x
    # No output may contain the absolute source path.
    for f in "$out"/placeholder.o "$out"/placeholder.elf; do
        if grep -q -F "$src" "$f"; then
            echo "FAIL: $f contains the source path $src" >&2; exit 1
        fi
    done
    (cd "$out" && find . -type f ! -name SHA256SUMS | sed 's|^\./||' \
        | LC_ALL=C sort | xargs sha256sum > SHA256SUMS)
}

case "${1:-}" in
    image) cmd_image ;;
    image-tag) image_tag ;;
    build) shift; cmd_build "$@" ;;
    inside) shift; cmd_inside "$@" ;;
    *) sed -n '5,12p' "$0" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac
# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1.10@sha256:865e5dd094beca432e8c0a1d5e1c465db5f998dca4e439981029b3b81fb39ed5
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
#
# Build container: Debian bookworm-slim (amd64, pinned by digest), packages
# from a pinned snapshot.debian.org date, and JieLi's toolchain downloaded
# and checked against the SHA-256 recorded in docs/TOOLCHAIN.md.
# The toolchain is never committed or published; it only exists inside
# locally built images.

ARG BASE=debian:bookworm-slim@sha256:ec31d744f83f4a73447ba045aaab9409997efe5cc706eca4890c1be36cc1606a

FROM --platform=linux/amd64 ${BASE} AS fetch
ARG SNAPSHOT=20261020T000000Z
ARG TOOLCHAIN_NAME=jieli-linux-toolchains-20250324.1
ARG TOOLCHAIN_URL=https://jl-update.oss-cn-shenzhen.aliyuncs.com/jieli-linux-toolchains-20250324.1.tar.xz
ARG TOOLCHAIN_SHA256=f686586bcfb45e0f0bb27fd2b39c7a7f313cb4f0e88a66a14da621ffa8225958
RUN rm -f /etc/apt/sources.list.d/debian.sources \
 && echo "deb [check-valid-until=no] http://snapshot.debian.org/archive/debian/${SNAPSHOT} bookworm main" > /etc/apt/sources.list \
 && apt-get -o Acquire::Retries=5 update \
 && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends ca-certificates curl xz-utils \
 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
RUN curl -fsSL --retry 5 --retry-all-errors --connect-timeout 60 -o /tmp/toolchain.tar.xz "${TOOLCHAIN_URL}" \
 && echo "${TOOLCHAIN_SHA256}  /tmp/toolchain.tar.xz" | sha256sum -c - \
 && mkdir -p /opt \
 && tar -xJf /tmp/toolchain.tar.xz -C /opt \
      "${TOOLCHAIN_NAME}/common" "${TOOLCHAIN_NAME}/pi32v2" \
 && mv "/opt/${TOOLCHAIN_NAME}" /opt/jieli \
 && rm /tmp/toolchain.tar.xz

FROM --platform=linux/amd64 ${BASE}
ARG SNAPSHOT=20261020T000000Z
RUN rm -f /etc/apt/sources.list.d/debian.sources \
 && echo "deb [check-valid-until=no] http://snapshot.debian.org/archive/debian/${SNAPSHOT} bookworm main" > /etc/apt/sources.list \
 && apt-get -o Acquire::Retries=5 update \
 && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends libstdc++6 zlib1g libtinfo6 \
 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
COPY --from=fetch /opt/jieli /opt/jieli
ENV PATH=/opt/jieli/pi32v2/bin:/opt/jieli/common/bin:/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin \
    SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=1767225600 \
    LC_ALL=C.UTF-8 \
    TZ=UTC
WORKDIR /src
firmware:
src

placeholder.c

#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
#
# Vendors the parts of JieLi's AC79 SDK we use, from a pinned commit, and
# checks every file against vendor/jieli-sdk/SHA256SUMS (PROVENANCE P-2).
#
#   tools/fetch-sdk.sh --verify   check the committed files (default, offline)
#   tools/fetch-sdk.sh --fetch    re-download them from the pinned commit into
#                                 vendor/jieli-sdk/, then verify
#
# To vendor another file: add its path to SDK_FILES, run --fetch, add its
# hash to SHA256SUMS in the same commit, and log it in PROVENANCE.md.
set -eu

SDK_URL=https://gitee.com/Jieli-Tech/fw-AC79_AIoT_SDK.git
SDK_COMMIT=5fa84a9b2f723a5e9337ad79dc2ad741fc98fe2d
SDK_FILES="
LICENSE
include_lib/driver/cpu/wl82/asm/WL82.h
include_lib/driver/cpu/wl82/asm/csfr.h
"

ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
DEST="$ROOT/vendor/jieli-sdk"
SUMS="$DEST/SHA256SUMS"

sha256() {
    if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then sha256sum "$1" | cut -d' ' -f1
    else shasum -a 256 "$1" | cut -d' ' -f1; fi
}

verify() {
    status=0
    # Every listed file must exist with the recorded hash...
    while read -r want path; do
        [ -n "$want" ] || continue
        if [ ! -f "$DEST/$path" ]; then
            echo "MISSING $path"; status=1; continue
        fi
        got=$(sha256 "$DEST/$path")
        if [ "$got" = "$want" ]; then echo "OK      $path"
        else echo "CHANGED $path ($got, want $want)"; status=1; fi
    done < "$SUMS"
    # ...and nothing else may be vendored under the SDK's paths.
    for f in $(cd "$DEST" && find . -type f ! -name SHA256SUMS ! -name SOURCE.md | sed 's|^\./||' | LC_ALL=C sort); do
        if ! awk -v p="$f" '$2 == p { found = 1 } END { exit !found }' "$SUMS"; then
            echo "UNLISTED $f"; status=1
        fi
    done
    for f in $SDK_FILES; do
        if ! awk -v p="$f" '$2 == p { found = 1 } END { exit !found }' "$SUMS"; then
            echo "NO HASH  $f (in SDK_FILES but not in SHA256SUMS)"; status=1
        fi
    done
    if [ $status -eq 0 ]; then echo "SDK files match commit $SDK_COMMIT"; fi
    return $status
}

fetch() {
    work=$(mktemp -d)
    trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
    git -C "$work" init -q
    git -C "$work" remote add origin "$SDK_URL"
    git -C "$work" fetch -q --depth 1 --filter=blob:none origin "$SDK_COMMIT"
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    git -C "$work" sparse-checkout set --no-cone $(for f in $SDK_FILES; do printf '/%s ' "$f"; done)
    git -C "$work" -c advice.detachedHead=false checkout -q FETCH_HEAD
    got=$(git -C "$work" rev-parse HEAD)
    [ "$got" = "$SDK_COMMIT" ] || { echo "fetched $got, want $SDK_COMMIT"; exit 1; }
    for f in $SDK_FILES; do
        mkdir -p "$DEST/$(dirname "$f")"
        cp "$work/$f" "$DEST/$f"
    done
    verify
}

case "${1:---verify}" in
    --verify) verify ;;
    --fetch) fetch ;;
    *) echo "usage: $0 [--verify|--fetch]" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac

#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
#
# Builds the harness's own test images with the pinned toolchain container
# (tools/build.sh image) and writes SHA256SUMS.
#
#   harness/tests/images/build.sh            build into this folder
#   harness/tests/images/build.sh --check    build into a temporary folder
#                                            and compare with the committed
#                                            images (C-HARNESS-IMAGES)
#   harness/tests/images/build.sh inside OUT (runs inside the container)
set -eu

HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd "$HERE/../../.." && pwd)
IMAGES="heartbeat halt wild hang console lcd leds keys pot midi audio flash"

inside() {
    out=$1
    cd "$HERE"
    flags="-target pi32v2 -std=c11 -ffreestanding -nostdlib -Os -Wall -Wextra -Werror"
    clang -target pi32v2 -c start.S -o "$out/start.o"
    for n in $IMAGES; do
        # shellcheck disable=SC2086
        clang $flags -c "$n.c" -o "$out/$n.o"
        ld -nostdlib -T image.ld -o "$out/$n.elf" "$out/start.o" "$out/$n.o"
        objcopy -O binary -j .text "$out/$n.elf" "$out/$n.bin"
        rm "$out/$n.o" "$out/$n.elf"
    done
    rm "$out/start.o"
    (cd "$out" && for n in $IMAGES; do sha256sum "$n.bin"; done > SHA256SUMS)
}

build() {
    out=$1
    sh "$ROOT/tools/build.sh" image >/dev/null
    tag=$(sh "$ROOT/tools/build.sh" image-tag)
    docker run --rm --platform linux/amd64 --network none --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" \
        -v "$ROOT:/src:ro" -v "$out:/out" "$tag" sh /src/harness/tests/images/build.sh inside /out
}

case "${1:-}" in
    inside) inside "$2" ;;
    --check)
        tmp=$(mktemp -d)
        trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT
        build "$tmp"
        if diff "$tmp/SHA256SUMS" "$HERE/SHA256SUMS" && (cd "$HERE" && sha256sum -c --quiet SHA256SUMS 2>/dev/null || shasum -a 256 -c --quiet SHA256SUMS); then
            echo "test images: rebuilt images match the committed ones"
        else
            echo "test images: FAIL, the committed images differ from a rebuild" >&2
            exit 1
        fi ;;
    "")
        tmp=$(mktemp -d)
        trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT
        build "$tmp"
        cp "$tmp"/*.bin "$tmp/SHA256SUMS" "$HERE/"
        cat "$HERE/SHA256SUMS" ;;
    *) sed -n '5,13p' "$0" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac
EOF
chmod +x build.sh && sh build.sh 2>&1 | tail -20

#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
#
# The harness's CI steps (spec side). tools/record.py runs them as the
# C-HARNESS-* checks, and skips them where harness/ isn't on disk.
#
#   harness/ci.sh tag                print the local image tag
#   harness/ci.sh image              build the runtime image (and print the
#                                    fwtest binary's SHA-256)
#   harness/ci.sh test               build the test stage: cargo test
#   harness/ci.sh suite OUT MOUNT    run tests/harness.suite in a fresh
#                                    container, harness/tests mounted
#                                    read-only at MOUNT; outputs in OUT
#   harness/ci.sh scope              the harness never uses the vendored
#                                    crates' update-package or stock-boot paths
#   harness/ci.sh context            write the build context (a tar) to stdout
set -eu

ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
PLATFORM=linux/amd64

sha256() {
    if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then sha256sum "$@"
    else shasum -a 256 "$@"; fi
}

# The image tag: a hash of everything that goes into the build context.
tag() {
    h=$(cd "$ROOT" && context_files | LC_ALL=C sort | while read -r f; do sha256 "$f"; done | sha256 | cut -c1-16)
    echo "small-beeps-fwtest:$h"
}

context_files() {
    git -C "$ROOT" ls-files vendor/emulator harness LICENSE NOTICE
}

# A tar of exactly the tracked context files, with fixed owners and times.
context() {
    cd "$ROOT"
    context_files | LC_ALL=C sort > "$tmp/files"
    tar --format=ustar -c -f - -T "$tmp/files" 2>/dev/null \
        || tar -c -f - $(cat "$tmp/files")
}

build() {
    target=$1 t=$2
    context | docker build --platform "$PLATFORM" --target "$target" -t "$t" -f harness/Dockerfile -
}

tmp=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT

case "${1:-}" in
    tag) tag ;;
    context) context ;;
    image)
        t=$(tag)
        build runtime "$t"
        docker image inspect --format 'image {{.Id}}' "$t"
        docker run --rm --platform "$PLATFORM" --network none --entrypoint sha256sum "$t" /usr/local/bin/fwtest
        docker run --rm --platform "$PLATFORM" --network none "$t" version ;;
    test)
        build test "$(tag)-test" ;;
    suite)
        out=$2 mount=$3
        t=$(tag)
        docker image inspect "$t" >/dev/null 2>&1 || build runtime "$t"
        rm -rf "$out"
        mkdir -p "$out"
        out=$(cd "$out" && pwd)
        docker run --rm --platform "$PLATFORM" --network none --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" \
            -v "$ROOT/harness/tests:$mount:ro" -v "$out:/out" "$t" \
            suite "$mount/harness.suite" --out /out/suite ;;
    scope)
        if grep -n -E 'fwsc|stock_from_package|stock_boot|write_boot_info|smk|Smk37|flaky' "$ROOT"/harness/src/*.rs; then
            echo "scope: FAIL, the harness names the update-package, stock-boot or other-board paths" >&2
            exit 1
        fi
        echo "scope: PASS (harness/src uses none of them)" ;;
    *) sed -n '5,18p' "$0" >&2; exit 2 ;;

#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
#
# Runs fwtest from its published container image, pinned by digest in
# config/fwtest-image (R-SEP-3). The firmware side uses the harness only
# this way: docs/HARNESS.md is the manual.
#
#   tools/fwtest run IMAGE --ms MS --out DIR [options]
#   tools/fwtest suite FILE --out DIR
#   tools/fwtest version
#   tools/fwtest --image          print the pinned image reference
#
# The current directory is mounted read-only at /work, and every path
# argument must be inside it (relative, or absolute under it). The --out
# folder is created on the host and mounted read-write on its own. The
# container runs as linux/amd64 with no network, as your user. After a run,
# DIR/runner.txt names the image used, for the record.
#
# FWTEST_IMAGE overrides the pinned image (spec side, to try a local build);
# runner.txt then says the image was not the pinned one.
set -eu

ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
PIN_FILE="$ROOT/config/fwtest-image"
pinned=$(grep -v '^#' "$PIN_FILE" | grep . | head -1)

if [ -n "${FWTEST_IMAGE:-}" ]; then
    ref=$FWTEST_IMAGE
    note="not the pinned image (FWTEST_IMAGE); pinned: $pinned"
else
    case "$pinned" in
        *@sha256:????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????) ;;
        *) echo "tools/fwtest: no published image is pinned yet (config/fwtest-image: $pinned)" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    esac
    ref=$pinned
    note="pinned (config/fwtest-image)"
fi

if [ "${1:-}" = "--image" ]; then
    echo "$ref"
    exit 0
fi

cwd=$(pwd -P)
inside() {
    # a path argument as the container sees it, or an error if it is outside cwd
    case "$1" in
        /*) p=$1 ;;
        *) p="$cwd/$1" ;;
    esac
    d=$(dirname "$p")
    if [ -d "$d" ]; then p="$(cd "$d" && pwd -P)/$(basename "$p")"; fi
    case "$p" in
        "$cwd") echo /work ;;
        "$cwd"/*) echo "/work/${p#"$cwd"/}" ;;
        *) echo "tools/fwtest: $1 is outside the current directory" >&2; return 1 ;;
    esac
}

out=""
set_out=0
args=""
quote() { printf "'%s'" "$(printf '%s' "$1" | sed "s/'/'\\\\''/g")"; }
first=1
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    a=$1
    shift
    if [ "$set_out" = 1 ]; then
        out=$a
        args="$args $(quote /out)"
        set_out=0
        continue
    fi
    case "$a" in
        --out) set_out=1; args="$args $(quote "$a")" ;;
        --*|run|suite|version|help) args="$args $(quote "$a")" ;;
        *)
            if [ "$first" = 1 ]; then args="$args $(quote "$a")"
            elif printf '%s' "$a" | grep -q '[/.]' && [ -e "$a" ] || [ -e "$(dirname "$a")" ] && printf '%s' "$a" | grep -q '/'; then
                args="$args $(quote "$(inside "$a")")"
            else args="$args $(quote "$a")"; fi ;;
    esac
    first=0
done

mounts="-v $(quote "$cwd"):/work:ro"
if [ -n "$out" ]; then
    case "$out" in /*) ;; *) out="$cwd/$out" ;; esac
    if [ -e "$out" ] && [ -n "$(ls -A "$out" 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
        echo "tools/fwtest: --out $out is not empty" >&2
        exit 2
    fi
    mkdir -p "$out"
    out=$(cd "$out" && pwd -P)
    mounts="$mounts -v $(quote "$out"):/out"
fi

set +e
eval docker run --rm --platform linux/amd64 --network none --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" \
    "$mounts" -w /work "$(quote "$ref")" "$args"
code=$?
set -e
if [ -n "$out" ]; then
    printf 'image: %s\nstatus: %s\nexit: %d\n' "$ref" "$note" "$code" > "$out/runner.txt"
fi
exit $code

#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
#
# C-CLEAN-FOLDER (R-CLEAN-1, R-SEP-2): makes a fresh clean folder with
# tools/clean-setup.sh from this checkout's HEAD, and checks that
#   - vendor/emulator/, harness/ and sessions/spec/ are not on disk;
#   - none of their files' contents are in its .git (a blob-less clone that
#     never fetched them);
#   - its live settings are config/claude/clean.json, which denies reading
#     all three, and the session banner says OK;
#   - its .git/info/attributes marks all three -diff.
# It never reads those folders' contents itself: only their file lists and
# object IDs, from this checkout's history.
set -eu

ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
EXCLUDED="vendor/emulator harness sessions/spec"
work=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
fail=0
bad() { echo "FAIL: $*"; fail=1; }

head=$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse HEAD)
# A bare copy that serves partial clones (a plain local clone would copy every
# object and ignore --filter).

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
"""tools/fwtest runs an image pinned by digest (R-SEP-3, R-HARN-10; check
C-FWTEST-PIN).

  check-fwtest-pin.py

config/fwtest-image must hold one image reference of the form
`ghcr.io/<owner>/<repository>@sha256:<64 hex digits>`, with no quiet words
in it (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Low profile"), or `unpublished` until the first
image is published (tools/fwtest then refuses to run). tools/fwtest must
take the image from that file, check for the digest form, and run it with
no network, as linux/amd64, with the working folder mounted read-only.
"""
import os
import re
import sys

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
REF = re.compile(r"^ghcr\.io/[a-z0-9-]+/[a-z0-9._-]+@sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$")
QUIET = re.compile(r"fm-?1|m-?vave|jie-?li|synth|firmware", re.I)
WRAPPER_MUST = [
    'PIN_FILE="$ROOT/config/fwtest-image"',
    "*@sha256:" + "?" * 64 + ")",
    "--network none",
    "--platform linux/amd64",
    ':/work:ro"',
]


def pinned(text):
    lines = [l.strip() for l in text.splitlines() if l.strip() and not l.startswith("#")]
    return lines[0] if len(lines) == 1 else None


def check(root=ROOT):
    problems = []
    with open(os.path.join(root, "config", "fwtest-image"), encoding="utf-8") as f:
        ref = pinned(f.read())
    if ref is None:
        problems.append("config/fwtest-image must hold exactly one reference")
    elif ref == "unpublished":
        print("config/fwtest-image: unpublished (no image yet; tools/fwtest refuses to run)")
    elif not REF.match(ref):
        problems.append("config/fwtest-image is not ghcr.io/<owner>/<repo>@sha256:<digest>: %s" % ref)
    elif QUIET.search(ref):
        problems.append("config/fwtest-image names a quiet word")
    else:
        print("config/fwtest-image: %s" % ref)
    with open(os.path.join(root, "tools", "fwtest"), encoding="utf-8") as f:
        wrapper = f.read()
    for must in WRAPPER_MUST:
        if must not in wrapper:
            problems.append("tools/fwtest lacks %r" % must)
    return problems


def main():
    problems = check()
    for p in problems:
        print("FAIL " + p)
    print("fwtest pin: %s" % ("FAIL" if problems else "PASS"))
    return 1 if problems else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

    with open(os.path.join(root, "config", "fwtest-image"), encoding="utf-8") as f:
        ref = pinned(f.read())
    if ref is None:
        problems.append("config/fwtest-image must hold exactly one reference")
    elif ref == "unpublished":
        print("config/fwtest-image: unpublished (no image yet; tools/fwtest refuses to run)")
    elif not REF.match(ref):
        problems.append("config/fwtest-image is not ghcr.io/<owner>/<repo>@sha256:<digest>: %s" % ref)
    elif QUIET.search(ref):
        problems.append("config/fwtest-image names a quiet word")
    else:
        print("config/fwtest-image: %s" % ref)
    with open(os.path.join(root, "tools", "fwtest"), encoding="utf-8") as f:
        wrapper = f.read()
    for must in WRAPPER_MUST:
        if must not in wrapper:
            problems.append("tools/fwtest lacks %r" % must)
    return problems

    for p in problems:
        print("FAIL " + p)
    print("fwtest pin: %s" % ("FAIL" if problems else "PASS"))
    return 1 if problems else 0

import shutil

import sys
import tempfile
import unittest

from tests.helpers import ROOT, load_tool

rec = load_tool("record.py")


class RecordTest(unittest.TestCase):
    """Requirements: R-PROC-4, R-REC-1"""

    def test_every_check_names_known_requirements(self):
        known = {r["id"] for r in rec.requirements_table()}
        self.assertTrue(known)
        ids = [c["id"] for c in rec.CHECKS]
        self.assertEqual(len(ids), len(set(ids)), "duplicate check IDs")
        for c in rec.CHECKS:
            self.assertTrue(c["reqs"], c["id"])
            for r in c["reqs"]:
                self.assertIn(r, known, "%s names unknown %s" % (c["id"], r))

    def test_requirements_table_names_only_real_checks(self):
        ids = {c["id"] for c in rec.CHECKS}
        for r in rec.requirements_table():
            for named in re.findall(r"C-[A-Z-]+[A-Z]", r["checked_by"]):
                self.assertIn(named, ids, "%s names unknown check %s" % (r["id"], named))

    def test_every_test_class_names_its_requirements(self):
        for path in glob.glob(os.path.join(ROOT, "tests", "test_*.py")):
            with open(path) as f:
                text = f.read()
            classes = re.findall(r'^class \w+\(unittest\.TestCase\):\n    """([^"]*)"""', text, re.M)
            self.assertTrue(classes, "%s: test classes need a docstring" % path)
            for doc in classes:
                self.assertRegex(doc, r"Requirements: R-[A-Z]+-\d+", path)

    def test_traceability(self):
        defined = [{"id": "C-X", "reqs": ["R-PROC-1"]},
                   {"id": "C-Y", "reqs": ["R-PROC-1", "R-PUB-1"]},
                   {"id": "C-Z", "reqs": ["R-PUB-2", "R-LIC-1"]},
                   {"id": "C-W", "reqs": ["R-LIC-1"]}]
        ran = [{"id": "C-X", "result": "PASS"}, {"id": "C-Y", "result": "FAIL"},
               {"id": "C-W", "result": "PASS"}]
        table = {t["requirement"]: t for t in rec.traceability(ran, defined)}
        self.assertEqual(table["R-PROC-1"]["result"], "FAIL")
        self.assertEqual(table["R-PROC-1"]["checks"], ["C-X", "C-Y"])
        self.assertEqual(table["R-PUB-1"]["result"], "FAIL")
        self.assertEqual(table["R-PUB-2"]["result"], "not run in this record (C-Z)")
        self.assertEqual(table["R-LIC-1"]["result"], "PASS (C-Z not run)")
        self.assertTrue(table["R-BOOT-1"]["result"].startswith("not machine-checked"))

    def test_run_writes_a_complete_record(self):
        out = tempfile.mkdtemp()
        try:
            p = subprocess.run([sys.executable, os.path.join(ROOT, "tools", "record.py"), "run",
                                "--out", out, "--only", "C-DENY-LISTS,C-SDK-PIN"],
                               cwd=ROOT, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, universal_newlines=True)
            self.assertEqual(p.returncode, 0, p.stdout)
            with open(os.path.join(out, "report.json")) as f:
                report = json.load(f)
            self.assertEqual([c["id"] for c in report["checks"]], ["C-DENY-LISTS", "C-SDK-PIN"])
            self.assertEqual(report["overall"], "PASS")
            self.assertIn("traceability", report)
            for name in ("report.md", "logs/C-DENY-LISTS.log", "SHA256SUMS"):
                self.assertTrue(os.path.exists(os.path.join(out, name)), name)
            sums = rec.read_sums(os.path.join(out, "SHA256SUMS"))
            self.assertIn("report.json", sums)
            self.assertEqual(sums["report.json"], rec.sha256_file(os.path.join(out, "report.json")))
        finally:
            shutil.rmtree(out)

        self.assertNotIn(word, terms.h(word))

sed -i '' 's/    timeout-minutes: 45/    timeout-minutes: 75/' .github/workflows/ci.yml && sed -i '' 's/    timeout-minutes: 60/    timeout-minutes: 90/' .github/workflows/records.yml && grep -n timeout .github/workflows/*.yml && cat > .github/workflows/fwtest-image.yml <<'EOF'
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
#
# Publishes the fwtest container image (spec side's harness, R-SEP-3) to
# GHCR, for every push to main that changes what goes into it. It builds
# with harness/ci.sh exactly as CI does, pushes it under this repository's
# name with the tag fwtest-<commit>, and prints the digest. A pull request
# then puts that digest in config/fwtest-image; tools/fwtest runs only the
# pinned digest, never a tag.
name: fwtest-image

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - "harness/**"
      - "vendor/emulator/**"
      - "LICENSE"
      - "NOTICE"
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  packages: write

concurrency:
  group: fwtest-image
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  publish:
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 45
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Build the image
        run: sh harness/ci.sh image

      - name: Push it and print its digest
        env:
          TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          ACTOR: ${{ github.actor }}
        run: |
          set -eu
          repo=$(printf '%s' "ghcr.io/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" | tr 'A-Z' 'a-z')
          local_tag=$(sh harness/ci.sh tag)
          remote="$repo:fwtest-$GITHUB_SHA"
          printf '%s' "$TOKEN" | docker login ghcr.io -u "$ACTOR" --password-stdin
          docker tag "$local_tag" "$remote"
          docker push "$remote"

# fwtest: the harness, as a black box

`fwtest` runs a raw image on an emulated board for a given number of
emulated milliseconds, feeds it timed inputs, and saves what it did:
memory, the screen, the LEDs, the flash chip, the audio, instruction counts.
It is the firmware side's only window into the emulator, and this page is
its whole manual. It says what fwtest does, not how the emulator does it.
Facts about the chip itself (registers, pins, timings, the panel's layout)
belong in `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`; ask for one through docs/SPEC-REQUESTS.md.

fwtest is a model. Where it and `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` disagree, the spec is the
authority on the hardware; report the difference as a spec request.

## Running it

The firmware side runs fwtest only through `tools/fwtest`, which runs the
published container image pinned by digest in `config/fwtest-image`
(R-SEP-3). It needs Docker; the image runs as linux/amd64 on any host.

```sh
tools/fwtest run out/build/app.bin --ms 100 --out out/t1 --ram 0x01c00000:64@end
tools/fwtest suite tests/fw/boot.suite --out out/suite
tools/fwtest version
tools/fwtest --image        # the pinned image reference
```

- Run it from the repository root. The current folder is mounted read-only,
  so every input path (image, script, flash file, golden folder, suite) must
  be inside it. `--out` is created and mounted writable on its own, and must
  be empty or not exist yet.
- The container has no network and runs as your user.
- After a run, `tools/fwtest` adds `runner.txt` to the output folder, naming
  the image it ran and whether it was the pinned one. A test record that
  used fwtest names that image; every record also notes the pinned image in
  its environment.

## The raw image

| Rule | Value |
|------|-------|
| Format | A flat binary: the bytes of the code window, from its first byte. No header, no ELF. |
| Load address | The image's first byte is at `0x02000000`, the start of the code window. Link it there. |
| Entry | Core 0 starts at `0x02000000`: the image's first instruction. |
| Size | 1 byte to 1 032 192 bytes (1 MiB less 16 KiB). |
| The flash chip | 1 MiB. Erased (all `0xFF`) unless `--flash FILE` gives its first bytes. The image is then written into it at offset `0x4000`, as an installed image sits. |
| Past the image | Reads in the code window after the image's last byte show the flash chip: window address `0x02000000 + n` shows chip offset `0x4000 + n`. Changes the image makes to the chip (erase, program) show through the window, also over the image's own bytes. |
| Writes to the window | Ignored (and listed as unmodelled accesses). |
| RAM | 1 MiB at `0x01C00000`, all zero at the start. Other memories, and what the real chip has: `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`. |
| Core 0 at the start | User mode. Every register is 0, both stack pointers included (set your own stacks first), except `r0` = `0x01C7FC00`: a 64-byte block of zeros whose first word holds `0x01C7FC40`. |
| Core 1 | Does not run until the image releases it (`HARDWARE-SPEC.md` says how). Then it runs alongside core 0. |

## Time

- Emulated time starts at 0 when the image starts. One instruction of core 0
  takes one cycle; there are 240 000 cycles in an emulated millisecond.
- When core 0 waits (the wait-for-interrupt instruction, or a tight loop
  outside an interrupt handler that does nothing but read the chip's
  free-running timer), time jumps ahead to the next timed event: the next
  interrupt source, script event or capture. Waiting therefore costs (almost)
  no instructions, and instruction counts measure work.
- Everything happens at exact emulated times. Captures and checks are taken
  at the first instruction boundary at or after the time asked; fwtest stops
  to look at least every 1024 core-0 instructions, and exactly at each
  capture time while core 0 is busy.

## The command line

```
fwtest run IMAGE --ms MS --out DIR [options]
fwtest suite FILE --out DIR
fwtest version
```

`run` options:

| Option | What it does |
|--------|--------------|
| `--ms MS` | Run for MS emulated milliseconds (up to three decimals). Required. |
| `--out DIR` | Write the outputs here. Required; must be empty or new. |
| `--script FILE` | Timed inputs (below). |
| `--flash FILE` | The flash chip's first bytes (at most 1 MiB); the rest is erased. |
| `--ram ADDR:LEN@WHEN` | Save LEN bytes of memory at ADDR at WHEN. Numbers in decimal, or hex with `0x`. Only RAM (main RAM and the other RAM banks `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` lists) can be saved; anything else is a usage error. Repeatable. |
| `--lcd WHEN` | Save the screen as a PNG at WHEN. Repeatable. |
| `--leds-every MS` | Sample the LEDs every MS into `leds.csv`. |
| `--flash-out` | Save the whole flash chip at the end (`flash.bin`). |
| `--wav` | Save the audio output (`audio.wav`). |
| `--ipb` | Save instructions per audio block (`ipb.csv`). |
| `--console` | Save the bytes written to the chip's debug message register (`console.txt`; `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` names it). |
| `--watchdog ADDR:MS` | A hang if the 32-bit word at RAM address ADDR stays the same for more than MS ms. |
| `--halt-ok` | A halt counts as success (exit 0). |
| `--golden DIR` | Compare the outputs with the golden files in DIR (below). |

WHEN is a time in ms (`10`, `2.5`) or `end`. The run ends at `--ms`, or
earlier on a fault, halt or hang; `end` captures are taken then.

## Input scripts

A text file, one event per line; `#` starts a comment. Times are emulated
milliseconds with up to three decimals. Events at the same time happen in
the order written.

```
# time   event
2        key 12 down
4        key 12 up
6        key 5 tap 3          # down at 6 ms, up at 9 ms (default hold: 50 ms)
10       enc 0 +2             # encoder 0, two detents clockwise
12       enc 3 -1             # one detent anticlockwise
15       pot 300              # the pot now reads 300
20       midi 90 3c 64        # bytes into the MIDI input, in this order
```

| Event | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `key N down`, `key N up` | Key N (0 to 40) pressed or released. |
| `key N tap [HOLD]` | Pressed, then released HOLD ms later (default 50). |
| `enc N +C`, `enc N -C` | Encoder N (0 to 6) turned C detents (1 to 1000); `+` is clockwise. A detent takes 8 ms to turn. |
| `pot V` | The pot's reading becomes V (0 to 1023). It reads 900 until a script sets it. |
| `midi HH ...` | Bytes (two hex digits each) arrive at the MIDI input one after another, at the wire's pace: one byte every 320 µs, the first 320 µs after the event's time. |

Key, LED and encoder numbers are fwtest's own. `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` maps them
to the panel and to the key matrix.

## Outputs

All in `--out`. A run writes only what it was asked for, plus
`result.json` and `junit.xml`.

| File | Contents |
|------|----------|
| `ram-AAAAAAAA-L-WHEN.bin` | The bytes saved by `--ram` (address as 8 hex digits, length in hex, WHEN as `10ms`, `2.500ms` or `end`). |
| `lcd-WHEN.png` | The screen, 240 x 240, 8-bit RGB, whatever the display's on/off state. Each pixel is the panel's 16-bit colour (5-6-5 bits) with each channel scaled to 8 bits (`c * 255 / 31`, or `/ 63` for green). |
| `leds.csv` | Header `ms,led0,...,led40`, then one row per sample: the sample's time, and for each LED the share of the time since the previous sample (or since the start) that it was lit, in thousandths (0 to 1000, rounded). LED N belongs to key N. |
| `flash.bin` | The flash chip (1 MiB) at the end of the run. |
| `audio.wav` | The audio output: 16-bit PCM, stereo, the header says 44 100 Hz. Every sample the output played, in order. How the firmware feeds the output, and its exact rate: `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`. |
| `ipb.csv` | Header `block,end_ms,core0,core1`, then one row per audio block (each time the output finished one half of its buffer): its number, the time it finished, and the instructions core 0 and core 1 executed since the previous block (the first row: since the start). Core 0's count is exact; core 1's is counted at a granularity of 1024 core-0 instructions. |
| `console.txt` | The debug console bytes, as written. |
| `result.json` | What happened (below). |
| `junit.xml` | JUnit XML: a test case `run` (fails on a fault or hang, and on a halt without `--halt-ok`), and one `golden NAME` per golden file. |

`result.json` holds: `fwtest` (version and the emulator build it carries),
`image` (file name, size, SHA-256), `script_sha256`, `run` (`outcome`,
`detail`, `emulated_ms`, `instructions` per core, `midi_bytes_dropped`,
`unmodelled_accesses`, and every output's name, size and SHA-256), `golden`
(each file's `match` or `mismatch` and why), and `exit_code`.

- `midi_bytes_dropped`: bytes that arrived while the image had no MIDI
  receiver set up, or more than about a second's worth waiting.
- `unmodelled_accesses`: addresses the image read or wrote that fwtest does
  not model (reads give 0, writes are dropped), with counts, up to 256.
  Usually a sign the image touched something unexpected; if the hardware
  has something there, ask for it in a spec request.

## Outcomes and exit codes

| Exit | Outcome | When |
|------|---------|------|
| 0 | completed | Ran for `--ms`, and every golden file matched. (Also a halt with `--halt-ok`.) |
| 1 | golden mismatch | A golden file differs (beyond its tolerance), or an output it names is missing. |
| 2 | usage error | Bad arguments, an unreadable or oversized image, a bad script, `--out` not empty, a capture outside RAM. Nothing ran. |
| 3 | fault | A core met an instruction it cannot decode or the emulator does not implement, or its program counter left every memory that can hold code (the image, RAM, the other RAM banks). |
| 4 | halt | Core 0 executed a jump to itself with interrupts disabled: a deliberate stop. The run ends there. |
| 5 | hang | The `--watchdog` word did not change for longer than its time. |

When several apply, the first in this order wins: 2, 3, 5, 1, 4, 0. Captures
and `result.json` are written for 1, 3, 4 and 5 too. Any other exit code
means fwtest itself failed.

## Golden files

`--golden DIR`: every file in DIR is a golden file, compared with the output
of the same name. A golden file without such an output is a mismatch. Outputs
without a golden file are not compared.

- **Exact by default:** byte for byte. Every fwtest output is deterministic,
  so exact is right unless the firmware's own behaviour is meant to vary.
- **Tolerances**, where an output is meant to be approximate: a text file
  `NAME.tolerance` beside the golden file, one line:
  - `pixel-diff N` (a `.png`): same size; each colour channel of each pixel
    within N.
  - `sample-diff N` (a `.wav`): same format and length; each sample within N.
  - `rel-percent P` (a `.csv`): same lines and fields; text fields equal;
    each integer within P percent of the golden value (at least 1). For
    example `ipb.csv` with `rel-percent 3` is the performance gate R-PERF-2
    will use.
- Golden PNG and WAV files compared with a tolerance must be ones fwtest
  wrote. To make a golden file, run once, check the output by hand, and copy
  it into the golden folder in the same commit as the test.

## Suites

`fwtest suite FILE --out DIR` runs several cases. Each line of FILE:

```
# NAME  EXPECT     IMAGE                 run options (paths relative to FILE)
boot    completed  ../out/build/app.bin  --ms 50 --ram 0x01c00000:16@end --golden golden/boot
stop    halt       images/stop.bin       --ms 10
```

NAME (letters, digits, `-`, `_`) is the case's output folder under DIR.
EXPECT is the outcome expected: `completed`, `halt`, `fault` or `hang`. A
case passes when its outcome is EXPECT and every golden file matches. DIR
also gets `result.json` (every case's result) and `junit.xml` (one test case
per suite case). The exit code is 0 when every case passes, 1 otherwise, 2
on a usage error.

## Determinism

The same image, script, options and fwtest build give byte-identical outputs
on every run and every machine: no host time, no randomness that isn't
seeded the same way every run, nothing from the environment, no host paths
in the results. CI runs the harness's own suite twice in fresh containers
and compares every output byte (C-HARNESS-DET). If two runs of yours ever
differ, that is a bug in fwtest: report it.

## Versions

`fwtest version` prints fwtest's version and the emulator build it carries;
`result.json` has both. The image is identified by its digest. When the
harness changes, a pull request moves `config/fwtest-image` to the new
digest, so a firmware test always names the exact runner it used.

emulated milliseconds, feeds it timed inputs, and saves what it did:
memory, the screen, the LEDs, the flash chip, the audio, instruction counts.
It is the firmware side's only window into the emulator, and this page is
its whole manual. It says what fwtest does, not how the emulator does it.
Facts about the chip itself (registers, pins, timings, the panel's layout)
belong in `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`; ask for one through docs/SPEC-REQUESTS.md.

fwtest is a model. Where it and `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` disagree, the spec is the
authority on the hardware; report the difference as a spec request.

## Running it

The firmware side runs fwtest only through `tools/fwtest`, which runs the
published container image pinned by digest in `config/fwtest-image`
(R-SEP-3). It needs Docker; the image runs as linux/amd64 on any host.

```sh
tools/fwtest run out/build/app.bin --ms 100 --out out/t1 --ram 0x01c00000:64@end
tools/fwtest suite tests/fw/boot.suite --out out/suite
tools/fwtest version
tools/fwtest --image        # the pinned image reference
```

- Run it from the repository root. The current folder is mounted read-only,
  so every input path (image, script, flash file, golden folder, suite) must
  be inside it. `--out` is created and mounted writable on its own, and must
  be empty or not exist yet.
- The container has no network and runs as your user.
- After a run, `tools/fwtest` adds `runner.txt` to the output folder, naming
  the image it ran and whether it was the pinned one. A test record that
  used fwtest names that image; every record also notes the pinned image in
  its environment.

| Load address | The image's first byte is at `0x02000000`, the start of the code window. Link it there. |
| Entry | Core 0 starts at `0x02000000`: the image's first instruction. |
| Size | 1 byte to 1 032 192 bytes (1 MiB less 16 KiB). |
| The flash chip | 1 MiB. Erased (all `0xFF`) unless `--flash FILE` gives its first bytes. The image is then written into it at offset `0x4000`, as an installed image sits. |
| Past the image | Reads in the code window after the image's last byte show the flash chip: window address `0x02000000 + n` shows chip offset `0x4000 + n`. Changes the image makes to the chip (erase, program) show through the window, also over the image's own bytes. |
| Writes to the window | Ignored (and listed as unmodelled accesses). |
| RAM | 1 MiB at `0x01C00000`, all zero at the start. Other memories, and what the real chip has: `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`. |
| Core 0 at the start | User mode. Every register is 0, both stack pointers included (set your own stacks first), except `r0` = `0x01C7FC00`: a 64-byte block of zeros whose first word holds `0x01C7FC40`. |
| Core 1 | Does not run until the image releases it (`HARDWARE-SPEC.md` says how). Then it runs alongside core 0. |

  takes one cycle; there are 240 000 cycles in an emulated millisecond.

  outside an interrupt handler that does nothing but read the chip's
  free-running timer), time jumps ahead to the next timed event: the next
  interrupt source, script event or capture. Waiting therefore costs (almost)
  no instructions, and instruction counts measure work.
- Everything happens at exact emulated times. Captures and checks are taken
  at the first instruction boundary at or after the time asked; fwtest stops
  to look at least every 1024 core-0 instructions, and exactly at each
  capture time while core 0 is busy.

# Spec requests

How the firmware side (clean) asks the spec side (exposed) for a hardware
fact it needs, and how the answer comes back, without anything else passing
between them (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Roles").

Don't ask how another firmware does something, and don't paste or describe
any material you aren't allowed to read. A question about fwtest's
behaviour (a capture, an exit code, an option) is not a spec request: open
an issue or a pull request against docs/HARNESS.md.

## Answering (spec side)

- Answer by adding the fact to `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`, with its source, as
  every fact there has (M0c's rules: facts only, never code or code

harness: the fwtest library and CLI

What:    harness/ is a Rust package (library plus the fwtest CLI) around
         the vendored emulator crates: it boots a raw image, runs it for a
         number of emulated milliseconds with a timed input script, takes
         the captures asked for (RAM, LCD as PNG, LEDs, flash, WAV,
         instructions per audio block, debug console), detects faults,
         halts and hangs, compares golden files with documented
         tolerances, and writes result.json and junit.xml; `suite` runs
         several cases. Rust is pinned to 1.99.0; PROVENANCE P-8.
Why:     M0b section 3; R-HARN-1 to R-HARN-7.
How:     No third-party crates: PNG (stored blocks), WAV, JSON, JUnit and
         SHA-256 are written by hand, so Cargo.lock lists path crates only
         and the build needs no registry. Determinism by construction: the
         emulator's native code generation stays off, time skips over
         waits so instruction counts measure work, outputs carry no host
         time or paths, and the process clears the environment variables
         that would change the emulator's behaviour. The upstream input
         format and key names are not used; the script format is fwtest's
         own.
Result:  cargo build --release: OK (warnings only in vendored code); unit
         tests in the next commits pass.
Sources: P-7, P-8

EOF

         behaviour, not from any probe or firmware of the upstream

#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
#
# Rebuilds a commit in its own pinned container and compares the outputs'
# SHA-256s with that commit's test record (R-REPRO-4).
#
#   tools/reproduce <commit> [--records-ref REF]
#
# The record comes from the `records` branch (fetched from origin, or a local
# branch of that name, or REF). The commit's files are exported with
# `git archive` into a temporary folder, so the build uses that commit's own
# Dockerfile and build script, and nothing from your working tree. In a
# blob-less clean clone, git may download the commit's other files to do
# this; the spec-side folders are excluded.
set -eu

[ $# -ge 1 ] || { echo "usage: $0 <commit> [--records-ref REF]" >&2; exit 2; }
ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
commit=$1
ref=""
[ "${2:-}" = "--records-ref" ] && ref=${3:-}

full=$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --verify "$commit^{commit}")
work=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT

if [ -z "$ref" ]; then
    if git -C "$ROOT" fetch -q origin records 2>/dev/null; then ref=FETCH_HEAD
    else ref=records; fi
fi
if ! git -C "$ROOT" show "$ref:records/$full/report.json" > "$work/report.json" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "no record for $full on $ref" >&2
    exit 1
fi
echo "commit:  $full"
echo "record:  $ref:records/$full/report.json"

mkdir "$work/src"
# Spec-side folders aren't needed to build, and must not land on a clean
# machine (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Barriers").
git -C "$ROOT" archive "$full" -- . ':(exclude)vendor/emulator' ':(exclude)harness' \
    | tar -x -C "$work/src"
sh "$work/src/tools/build.sh" build --out "$work/out"
"$(sh "$ROOT/tools/find-python.sh")" -I "$ROOT/tools/record.py" compare --record "$work/report.json" --outputs "$work/out"

#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
#
# Updates a clean folder to its remote's main (or REF), the safe way.
#
#   tools/clean-update.sh [REF]
#
# Clean sessions run with git's lazy fetching off (GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1, set
# by config/claude/clean.json), so no command can download a file the clean
# folder leaves out. A checkout of new commits needs lazy fetching for the
# files it does check out, so this script allows it for exactly one
# fast-forward, then re-applies the sparse checkout and checks that no file
# under vendor/emulator/, harness/ or sessions/spec/ reached the disk or the
# folder's .git. Stop and tell the owner if it fails.
set -eu

ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
ref=${1:-main}
role=$(cat "$ROOT/.claude/small-beeps-role" 2>/dev/null || true)
[ "$role" = clean ] || { echo "clean-update.sh is for clean folders (role here: ${role:-none})" >&2; exit 2; }

GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 git -C "$ROOT" fetch -q origin
env -u GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH git -C "$ROOT" merge -q --ff-only "origin/$ref"
GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 sh "$ROOT/tools/clean-setup.sh" > /dev/null

fail=0
for p in vendor/emulator harness sessions/spec; do
    [ ! -e "$ROOT/$p" ] || { echo "STOP: $p is on disk"; fail=1; }
    have=$(GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 git -C "$ROOT" ls-tree -r HEAD -- "$p" | awk '$2 == "blob" { print $3 }' \
        | GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 git -C "$ROOT" cat-file --batch-check='%(objectname)' 2>/dev/null | grep -vc missing || true)
    [ "$have" = 0 ] || { echo "STOP: $have file(s) under $p are in .git"; fail=1; }
done
if [ $fail -ne 0 ]; then echo "Tell the owner before doing anything else." >&2; exit 1; fi
echo "clean folder at $(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --short HEAD); no spec-side files on disk or in .git"
EOF
chmod +x tools/clean-update.sh; python3 tools/check-deny-lists.py | tail -1; python3 -m unittest tests.test_deny_lists 2>&1 | tail -1

You have access to browser automation tools (mcp__claude-in-chrome__*) for interacting with web pages in Chrome. Follow these guidelines for effective browser automation.

If you are looking for specific log entries, use the 'pattern' parameter with a regex-compatible pattern. This filters results efficiently and avoids overwhelming output. IMPORTANT: Do not trigger JavaScript alerts, confirms, prompts, or browser modal dialogs through your actions. These browser dialogs block all further browser events and will prevent the extension from receiving any subsequent commands. 3. Use mcp__claude-in-chrome__javascript_tool to check for and dismiss any existing dialogs before proceeding

If you accidentally trigger a dialog and lose responsiveness, inform the user they need to manually dismiss it in the browser.

## Avoid rabbit holes and loops

When using browser automation tools, stay focused on the specific task. If you encounter any of the following, stop and ask the user for guidance:
- Unexpected complexity or tangential browser exploration
- Browser tool calls failing or returning errors after 2-3 attempts
- No response from the browser extension
- Page elements not responding to clicks or input
- Pages not loading or timing out

Explain what you attempted, what went wrong, and ask how the user would like to proceed. Do not keep retrying the same failing browser action or explore unrelated pages without checking in first.

## Tab context and session startup

IMPORTANT: At the start of each browser automation session, call mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp first to get information about the user's current browser tabs. Use this context to understand what the user might want to work with before creating new tabs.

Never reuse tab IDs from a previous/other session. Follow these guidelines:
1. Only reuse an existing tab if the user explicitly asks to work with it
2. Otherwise, create a new tab with mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp
3. If a tool returns an error indicating the tab doesn't exist or is invalid, call tabs_context_mcp to get fresh tab IDs
4. When a tab is closed by the user or a navigation error occurs, call tabs_context_mcp to see what tabs are available
